mainTopic: בעל אוב and ידעוני: why the משנה in כריתות lists only the בעל אוב, and what counts as an action for a קרבן
overview: The משנה defines two kinds of sorcerers, the בעל אוב and the ידעוני. It rules that both get סקילה, and that a person who consults them breaks a לאו. The גמרא asks why the משנה in כריתות lists only the בעל אוב. רבי יוחנן answers that both share one לאו. ריש לקיש answers that the ידעוני does no action. The גמרא tests each answer and explains why each אמורא did not accept the other's. This leads to a discussion of how small a movement can count as an action: twisting the lips, striking the arms, or bowing, according to רבי עקיבא and according to the רבנן. To explain why the רבנן do not exempt the בעל אוב, עולא, רבא and אביי argue about which case the משנה means. Their discussion ends with a בעל אוב who burns incense to gather demons. A side ברייתא about חובר חבר follows. Finally, רבא explains that the מגדף is different because his sin is in the heart.

steps.title: The משנה defines the two sorcerers and their punishment
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines בעל אוב and ידעוני. Both are punished with סקילה, and the person who consults them breaks a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בעל אוב is a פיתום who makes a voice speak from his armpit. A ידעוני is one who makes a voice speak from his mouth. Both are stoned, and a person who asks them questions breaks a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of people who get סקילה. It adds two kinds of sorcerers and explains how each one works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate people are described here: the בעל אוב, whose voice seems to come from his armpit, and the ידעוני, whose voice comes from his mouth. The sorcerers themselves get the death penalty. The customer who consults them only breaks a לאו and does not get סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A necromancer whose voice comes from his armpit
A sorcerer who speaks from his mouth
A warning, meaning a לאו (prohibition), but not a death penalty

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two people. The sorcerer gets סקילה, but the one who asks him questions only breaks a לאו.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A necromancer — this is a pitom
phrases.notes: פיתום is the name for this kind of sorcerer. The next words explain what he does.

phrases.english: who speaks from his armpit,
and a sorcerer — this is one who speaks with his mouth.
These are put to death by stoning,
and one who inquires through them is under a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל אוֹב – זֶה פִּיתוֹם הַמְדַבֵּר מִשֶּׁחְיוֹ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בעל אוב and ידעוני are both stoned. One who consults them breaks a לאו.

steps.title: Why does the משנה in כריתות leave out the ידעוני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that our משנה lists both sorcerers, while the משנה in מסכת כריתות lists only בעל אוב. It asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does our משנה list both בעל אוב and ידעוני, while the משנה in כריתות lists בעל אוב and leaves out ידעוני?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares our משנה with the list in כריתות and asks why ידעוני is missing there. This question sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in כריתות lists the sins that carry כרת. Since both sorcerers get סקילה here, we would expect both to appear in that list too. The question is what makes ידעוני different when it comes to the כריתות list.

keyTerms.meaning: The מסכת that lists sins punishable by כרת

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is different here,
that it teaches necromancer and sorcerer,
and what is different regarding Kereisos,
that it teaches necromancer
and leaves out the sorcerer?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּקָתָנֵי בַּעַל אוֹב וְיִדְּעוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the משנה's list with the parallel list in כריתות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why ידעוני is left out of the כריתות list even though it appears in our משנה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both sorcerers share one prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that ידעוני is not counted separately in כריתות because both sorcerers are forbidden in a single לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: since both of them were stated in one prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כריתות list counts separate prohibitions. The תורה forbids בעל אוב and ידעוני in one single לאו, so the list counts them as one item and names only בעל אוב. A ידעוני is still punished; he is simply not listed as a separate entry.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Since both of them were stated in one prohibition.
phrases.notes: So the list in כריתות counts them as one item, and naming בעל אוב covers both.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הוֹאִיל וּשְׁנֵיהֶן בְּלָאו אֶחָד נֶאֶמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two are counted as one because they are stated in one לאו

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the ידעוני does no action
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that ידעוני is left out of כריתות because his sin involves no physical action.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: ידעוני is left out because there is no action in it.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a second, different answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, the reason has nothing to do with how the פסוק is worded. The ידעוני only speaks, and a sin with no action is not included in the כריתות list. So the two אמוראים disagree about why ידעוני is missing.
steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons are given for why ידעוני is missing from כריתות: רבי יוחנן says it shares one לאו with בעל אוב, and ריש לקיש says it involves no action.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The sorcerer is left out because there is no action in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: יִדְּעוֹנִי, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer that disagrees with רבי יוחנן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ידעוני is omitted because the sin involves no action

steps.title: Why does the list name בעל אוב in particular?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבי יוחנן: if both sorcerers share one לאו, why does כריתות mention בעל אוב rather than ידעוני?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן, what is special about בעל אוב that the משנה chose to mention him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יוחנן's answer and asks a follow-up question. If the two sorcerers really count as one sin, why does the list name בעל אוב and not ידעוני?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, בעל אוב and ידעוני form one package under a single לאו. So the משנה could have named either one to stand for the package. The גמרא wants to know why it picked בעל אוב.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this one and not the other?
He took / he chose to mention
A necromancer, who speaks with the dead

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan,
what is different about the necromancer that it chose to mention him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מַאי שְׁנָא בַּעַל אוֹב דְּנָקֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוחנן's answer from step 3 and checks a detail of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the כריתות list chose בעל אוב to represent the shared לאו.

steps.title: The פסוק mentions בעל אוב first
steps.stepSummary: The משנה names בעל אוב because the פסוק lists him first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק opens with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה chose בעל אוב simply because the פסוק mentions him first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The choice has nothing to do with law. When two items share one לאו, it is natural to name the one the תורה lists first. That keeps רבי יוחנן's answer standing.

keyTerms.meaning: It opened with him / began with him

phrases.english: Because the verse begins with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דִּפְתַח בֵּיהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows the order of the פסוק, which lists בעל אוב first.

steps.title: Why didn't ריש לקיש accept רבי יוחנן's answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש did not simply say, like רבי יוחנן, that both sorcerers share one לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש, what is the reason he did not say like רבי יוחנן?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks why ריש לקיש did not just give רבי יוחנן's simple answer. This sets up רב פפא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'one לאו' answer looks simple and clean. If ריש לקיש needed a different reason, he must have seen a problem with it, and the גמרא wants to know what that problem is.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not say like... (he did not accept someone else's view)

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say like Rabbi Yoḥanan?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רבי יוחנן to asking about ריש לקיש's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What problem ריש לקיש saw in the 'one לאו' explanation.

steps.title: רב פפא: they have separate death penalties
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that ריש לקיש sees the two sorcerers as separate, because each has its own death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: they are separated with regard to the death penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains ריש לקיש's view. The two sorcerers are treated as separate sins when it comes to the death penalty, so they cannot be counted as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To ריש לקיש, a separate death penalty shows that these are two separate sins. That means each one should need its own קרבן חטאת. So the 'one לאו' answer does not explain why ידעוני is missing, and ריש לקיש needed the 'no action' reason instead.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
They are divided with regard to the death penalty.
phrases.notes: He means each sorcerer gets his own death penalty, so ריש לקיש sees them as two sins that would each need a קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: חֲלוּקִין הֵן בְּמִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the death penalties are separate, the two sins count separately, so 'one לאו' cannot explain why ידעוני is left out.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only a separate לאו counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that a separate לאו makes two sins for קרבנות, but a separate death penalty does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: a division by a לאו is called a division; a division by death penalty is not called a division.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוחנן's reply to רב פפא's point. For counting קרבנות, only separate לאוין matter, not separate death penalties.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree about what makes two sins count as two for a קרבן. רבי יוחנן says only the number of לאוין matters. Since there is just one לאו here, there is just one קרבן, so his answer still works.

keyTerms.meaning: A division made by a separate לאו
It is called / it counts as

steps.whatToRemember: The two sides disagree about what splits sins apart for קרבנות. רבי יוחנן says only a separate לאו does. ריש לקיש, as רב פפא explains him, says a separate death penalty also does.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan:
a division of a prohibition is considered a division,
a division of death penalty is not considered a division.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: חֲלוּקָּה דְּלָאו שְׁמָהּ חֲלוּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן rejects the basis of רב פפא's explanation in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that separate death penalties make two sins for קרבנות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For counting קרבנות, only separate לאוין count, not separate death penalties.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי יוחנן accept ריש לקיש's answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not say, like ריש לקיש, that ידעוני is missing because his sin has no action.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what is the reason he did not say like ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the opposite question: why didn't רבי יוחנן use ריש לקיש's 'no action' reason? This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that a קרבן חטאת comes only for a sin that involves an action. So ריש לקיש's reason looks strong, and the גמרא wants to know why רבי יוחנן did not use it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say like Reish Lakish?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 7, now asking about רבי יוחנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן rejected the 'no action' explanation.

steps.title: The כריתות משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the כריתות משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who does not require an action to bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: the משנה in כריתות is רבי עקיבא's view, and he says we do not need an action.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why he cannot use ריש לקיש's reason. The משנה in כריתות follows רבי עקיבא, and for רבי עקיבא a sin without an action can still need a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה does not require an action, then 'no action' cannot be why ידעוני is missing. So the 'one לאו' reason is the only one left. That is why רבי יוחנן holds on to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The מסכת that lists sins punished by כרת

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says ידעוני is missing because of the shared לאו. ריש לקיש says it is missing because there is no action. Each one has a reason for rejecting the other's explanation.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying that ידעוני's sin involves an action. He is saying that under רבי עקיבא's view, the lack of an action does not matter for bringing a קרבן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the disagreement depends on which תנא the כריתות משנה follows: whether a קרבן חטאת needs a physical action.

phrases.english: He could say to you:
the mishna of Karetot follows Rabbi Akiva,
who says: we do not require an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: מַתְנִיתִין דְּכָרֵיתוֹת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כריתות משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who does not require an action, so 'no action' cannot explain why ידעוני is left out.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: רבי עקיבא still needs a small action
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש would answer that רבי עקיבא does not need a big action, but he does need a small one. So the ידעוני, who does no action at all, is still left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש would say: true, רבי עקיבא does not need a big action, but he does need a small action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש did not accept רבי יוחנן's answer from step 11. In his view, even רבי עקיבא needs some small action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the כריתות משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who does not need an action at all. ריש לקיש splits it into two levels: רבי עקיבא gives up on a big action but still needs a small one. The ידעוני only speaks and does nothing, so he still has no action. That is why ריש לקיש's reason for leaving him out of the משנה still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that, even if (we accept this point)

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש does not disagree that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. He only says that רבי עקיבא's leniency has a limit: some small action is still needed.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish [would answer]:
Granted that Rabbi Akiva does not require
a big action,
a small action he does require.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּלָא בָּעֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַעֲשֶׂה רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רבי יוחנן's answer in step 11 by limiting רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that, according to רבי עקיבא, no action at all is needed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא only drops the need for a big action. He still needs a small one, which the ידעוני does not have.

steps.title: Challenge: what action does a blasphemer do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: a מגדף only speaks, so what small action does he do?
steps.simpleTranslation: A מגדף — what action is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's claim that רבי עקיבא needs a small action. The מגדף seems to have no action at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, a מגדף brings a קרבן even though his sin is only words. If רבי עקיבא really needed a small action, the מגדף should not bring one. This makes it look like רבי עקיבא needs no action at all, just as רבי יוחנן said.

phrases.english: A blasphemer — what action is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְגַדֵּף, מַאי מַעֲשֶׂה אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests ריש לקיש's new rule from step 12 against the case of the מגדף.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that רבי עקיבא needs at least a small action.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מגדף brings a קרבן according to רבי עקיבא even though he only speaks, so it seems no action is needed.

steps.title: Twisting the lips counts as an action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that when the מגדף speaks, the twisting of his lips counts as a small action.
steps.simpleTranslation: The twisting of his lips is an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש. Moving the lips while speaking counts as the small action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Speech is not just thought, because the lips physically move. That tiny movement is enough for the 'small action' רבי עקיבא needs. So the מגדף fits ריש לקיש's rule after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The twisting of his lips (when speaking)

phrases.english: The twisting of his lips counts as an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲקִימַת שְׂפָתָיו הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what counts as a small action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מגדף only speaks, so he does no action at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Moving the lips while speaking counts as a small action, which is enough for רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Challenge: what action does a necromancer do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the בעל אוב, who is also listed as bringing a קרבן: what action does he do?
steps.simpleTranslation: A בעל אוב — what action is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests ריש לקיש's rule again, this time on the בעל אוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כריתות משנה lists the בעל אוב as bringing a קרבן. If a small action is needed, the גמרא must show what his action is. Otherwise ריש לקיש's rule would not fit the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sorcerer who raises the dead to ask them questions

phrases.english: A necromancer — what action is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל אוֹב, מַאי מַעֲשֶׂה אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as step 13, now applied to the בעל אוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that a small action is needed, so the ידעוני is left out but the בעל אוב is included.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the בעל אוב also has no action, he should be left out just like the ידעוני.

steps.title: Striking the arms counts as an action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the בעל אוב strikes his arms together, and that counts as an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: The striking of his arms is an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש. The בעל אוב does a physical movement, striking his arms, so he has a small action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the real difference between the two sorcerers. The בעל אוב does something with his body, so he can bring a קרבן according to רבי עקיבא. The ידעוני only speaks, which is why ריש לקיש says he is left out of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The striking of his arms against each other

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, רבי עקיבא needs at least a small action. The מגדף has one (moving lips) and the בעל אוב has one (striking arms), but the ידעוני has none.

phrases.english: The striking of his arms counts as an action.
phrases.notes: He knocks his arms together to make a sound like a voice. That body movement is the action.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקָּשַׁת זְרוֹעוֹתָיו הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a physical action in the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בעל אוב does no action, just like the ידעוני.
steps.terutzMaskana: Striking his arms is a small action, so the בעל אוב brings a קרבן according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Would striking the arms count even for the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether striking the arms would count as an action even for the רבנן, and brings a ברייתא that only lists real actions like זיבוח, קיטור, ניסוך and השתחואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it an action even according to the רבנן? But a ברייתא teaches: a person is only liable for something that has an action, such as slaughtering, burning, pouring and bowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge: would the striking of the arms count as an action even for the רבנן? It begins by quoting a ברייתא about עבודה זרה. Together with the statements in the next two steps, this builds the challenge that is stated in full in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן require a real action to bring a קרבן. The ברייתא, speaking about עבודה זרה, lists only full actions: slaughtering, burning, pouring and bowing. Striking the arms does not look like that kind of action, so the גמרא questions whether it could satisfy the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who argue with רבי עקיבא and require a real action
Slaughtering, burning (incense) and pouring (a drink offering) — forms of worship

steps.confusionAlert: This is a question about the רבנן, not רבי עקיבא. Everything so far was about רבי עקיבא's view. Now the גמרא asks whether the same small action would also count for the רבנן.

phrases.english: And [is it an action] even according to the Rabbis? But isn't it taught:
phrases.notes: He means striking the arms: would even the רבנן, who need a real action, count it?

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: One is liable only for a matter that has an action in it,
such as slaughtering, burning, pouring, and bowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 16 (striking the arms is an action) and asks whether it also works for the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that striking the arms counts as an action even according to the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists bowing as an action. ריש לקיש says that only רבי עקיבא would count bowing (step 18). If even bending the whole body is not an action for the רבנן, then striking the arms surely is not one either (step 20).

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the ברייתא that counts bowing follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the ברייתא that lists bowing as an act of עבודה זרה follows רבי עקיבא, who does not require a real action.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: Who is the תנא who listed bowing? It is רבי עקיבא, who holds that we do not need a real action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting what was said about this ברייתא: ריש לקיש says it follows רבי עקיבא. This is not an answer. It is part of the setup for the challenge against ריש לקיש in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bowing is only a bending of the body, not a real physical action. ריש לקיש says it can only be counted by someone who does not require a real action, and that is רבי עקיבא. So in ריש לקיש's view, a small movement like this would not count for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (the teacher of this teaching)?
We do not require an action

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
Who is the tanna who taught bowing?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from the last step that lists bowing together with slaughtering, burning and pouring.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Akiva,
who says: We do not require an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מַאן תְּנָא הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted material of step 17. ריש לקיש's attribution of the ברייתא to רבי עקיבא is cited to support the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא (רבי עקיבא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא that lists bowing seemed to reflect everyone's view, including the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא only, since he does not require a real action.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: bending the body counts as an action even for the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and says the ברייתא can follow the רבנן, because bending one's body counts as an action for them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: You can even say the ברייתא follows the רבנן, because bending one's body is an action according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The quotation continues with רבי יוחנן's view, which disagrees with ריש לקיש: the ברייתא can match the רבנן too. The גמרא is still building toward the challenge in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two argue about how big a movement must be to count as an action for the רבנן. For רבי יוחנן, bending the body is enough. For ריש לקיש, it is not, so he had to say the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the רבנן

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
You may even say it follows the Rabbis,
since the bending of one's body is an action according to the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted dispute. רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש's statement in step 18 about who taught the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening the definition of an action so the ברייתא fits the רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bowing seemed too small to count as an action for the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוחנן, bending the body is a real action even for the רבנן.

steps.title: If bowing is not an action, how can striking the arms be one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: if bending the body is not an action for the רבנן, striking the arms of a בעל אוב should not be one either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, according to ריש לקיש, bending the body is not an action for the רבנן. So is the striking of the arms by a בעל אוב an action?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in ריש לקיש's views. His view on bowing seems to clash with what he said about the בעל אוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 16) the בעל אוב's striking of his arms was counted as an action. But bowing uses the whole body and is a bigger movement than striking the arms. If even bowing is not an action for the רבנן, striking the arms should surely not be one.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (used to build a 'how much more so' argument)

phrases.english: Now, according to Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: כְּפִיפַת קוֹמָתוֹ לְרַבָּנַן לָא הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: the bending of one's body is not an action according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּשַׁת זְרוֹעוֹתָיו דְּבַעַל אוֹב הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה?
phrases.english: so would the striking of the arms of a necromancer be an action?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to ריש לקיש's line (step 18) and tests it against step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that striking the arms counts as an action
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bowing is a bigger movement than striking the arms. If bowing is not an action for the רבנן, then striking the arms surely is not either.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's view on the בעל אוב was only according to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש counted striking the arms as an action only according to רבי עקיבא, not according to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ריש לקיש said striking the arms is an action, that too was according to רבי עקיבא. But according to the רבנן, it is not an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by limiting his earlier statement. It applies only to רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש is now consistent: for the רבנן, neither bowing nor striking the arms is an action. Both only count for רבי עקיבא, who does not need a real action.
steps.whatToRemember: For ריש לקיש, small movements like bowing or striking the arms count as an action only for רבי עקיבא, never for the רבנן.

phrases.english: When Reish Lakish said it, it too was
according to Rabbi Akiva,
but according to the Rabbis, it is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ נָמֵי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the statement to one תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש seemed to hold that striking the arms is an action for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Striking the arms is an action only for רבי עקיבא, not for the רבנן.

steps.title: Then the רבנן should have excluded both the מגדף and the בעל אוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the בעל אוב has no action for the רבנן, they should have listed him with the מגדף as someone who does not bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the רבנן should have said: 'This excludes the מגדף and the בעל אוב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the answer it just gave. If the רבנן hold that the בעל אוב does no action, their list of exclusions is missing him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן exclude the מגדף from bringing a קרבן because he does no action. If the בעל אוב also does no action for them, they should have excluded him too. Since they mention only the מגדף, it seems they do count the בעל אוב as doing an action.

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא מְגַדֵּף וּבַעַל אוֹב מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: he should have said: Excluding a blasphemer and a necromancer!
phrases.notes: This refers to the רבנן's teaching that the מגדף is left out of bringing a קרבן because he does no action.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, יָצָא מְגַדֵּף וּבַעַל אוֹב מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that for the רבנן the בעל אוב does no action
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן exclude only the מגדף for lacking an action. If the בעל אוב also lacked an action, they would have excluded him too, and they did not.

steps.title: עולא: The בעל אוב in the משנה burns incense to a demon
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers the question from step 22. The בעל אוב in the משנה in כריתות is someone who burns incense to a demon, and that is a real action even for the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, עולא said: The משנה is talking about one who burns incense to a demon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question of why the רבנן did not list the בעל אוב with the מגדף. עולא says the בעל אוב in that משנה is doing a real action: burning incense to a demon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a בעל אוב supposedly has no real action according to the רבנן, so he should be exempt from a קרבן like the מגדף. עולא changes the case. The בעל אוב in that משנה burns incense, and burning incense is clearly an action, so the רבנן have no reason to exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier approach is dropped and a new answer is coming.

phrases.english: Rather, עולא said:
It is talking about one who burns incense to a demon.
phrases.notes: He means the בעל אוב listed in the משנה in כריתות, the one the question in step 22 was about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22 by redefining which בעל אוב the משנה in כריתות means.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בעל אוב in the משנה has no real action according to the רבנן, so he should have been exempted with the מגדף.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בעל אוב there burns incense to a demon, which is a real action, so he does bring a קרבן.

steps.title: רבא: Burning incense to a demon is just idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to עולא. A person who burns incense to a demon is an עובד עבודה זרה, which is already its own entry in the משנה, so this cannot be the separate case of the בעל אוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: One who burns incense to a demon is an idol worshipper!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges עולא's answer. Burning incense to a demon is worship, so the person is simply an idol worshipper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in כריתות already lists עבודה זרה as its own item. If the בעל אוב were only someone burning incense to a demon, he would be the same as the idol worshipper, and there would be no reason to list him separately. So עולא's reading makes the בעל אוב entry pointless.

phrases.english: רבא said to him:
One who burns incense to a demon,
he is an idol worshipper!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מְקַטֵּר לַשֵּׁד עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks עולא's case definition from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that the בעל אוב in the משנה burns incense to a demon.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Burning incense to a demon is idol worship, which the משנה already lists. The בעל אוב entry would then be repetitive.

steps.title: רבא: He burns incense to gather the demons
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers his own answer. The בעל אוב in the משנה burns incense to gather the demons together, not to worship them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The משנה is talking about one who burns incense to gather the demons.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected עולא's answer, רבא gives his own. The person burns incense to draw demons together, as a kind of sorcery and not as worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps what was good in עולא's answer: burning incense is a real action, so the רבנן would not exempt him like the מגדף. It also fixes the problem from step 24. Because the incense is not offered as worship, this person is not simply an idol worshipper, so the בעל אוב entry stays separate.

keyTerms.meaning: To gather together, here meaning to bring the demons to one place.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
It is talking about one who burns incense to gather them.
phrases.notes: He is gathering the demons, not worshipping them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא בִּמְקַטֵּר לְחַבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting עולא's reading in step 24, רבא offers a new case definition that answers step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning incense to a demon counts as idol worship, so it cannot be the separate בעל אוב case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The incense is burned to gather demons, which is a real action but not worship.

steps.title: אביי: Gathering demons makes him a חובר חבר
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא. Someone who burns incense to gather demons is a חובר חבר, a charmer, which is a separate category from the בעל אוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: One who burns incense to gather is a charmer!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי objects to רבא's answer. Gathering demons sounds like the separate sin of חובר חבר, not like a בעל אוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists חובר חבר as its own forbidden act, separate from אוב. If רבא's person is really a חובר, then he does not belong in the בעל אוב entry of the משנה, which deals with a sin carrying a heavier punishment. So רבא's case seems to be in the wrong category.

keyTerms.meaning: A charmer, someone who gathers or binds through sorcery. The Torah forbids this separately.
אביי, רבא's colleague, who objects here.

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
One who burns incense to gather,
he is a charmer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי הַמְקַטֵּר לְחַבָּר חוֹבֵר חָבֵר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's case definition from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the בעל אוב in the משנה burns incense to gather demons.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gathering demons fits the separate Torah category of חובר חבר, not the category of בעל אוב.

steps.title: רבא: Yes, but the תורה gives this חובר סקילה
steps.stepSummary: רבא agrees that this person is a חובר, but says the תורה treats this particular חובר, the one who gathers demons, as liable to סקילה like a בעל אוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, he is a charmer, but the Torah said: This charmer is punished with stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי. He accepts that the person is a חובר, but says this specific kind of חובר is punished like a בעל אוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not deny אביי's point. He says the two categories overlap: a חובר who gathers demons is included in the punishment of the בעל אוב, which is סקילה. So he can still be the בעל אוב of the משנה, who does a real action and brings a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes. It admits the other person's point before adding a qualification.
But the Torah said. It introduces what the Torah teaches about this case.
Stoning, the death penalty for a בעל אוב.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the בעל אוב in the משנה in כריתות burns incense to gather demons. That is a real action, so even the רבנן agree he brings a קרבן. Although he is also a חובר, the תורה gives this kind of חובר סקילה.

phrases.english: Yes, but the Torah said:
This charmer is punished with stoning.
phrases.notes: "This" charmer means the one who gathers demons. He is punished like a בעל אוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין וְהַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה חוֹבֵר זֶה בִּסְקִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבא's case definition from step 25 against אביי's challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Conceding the point while qualifying it (the categories overlap)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A person who gathers demons is only a חובר חבר and cannot be the בעל אוב of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is a חובר, but the Torah gives this kind of חובר סקילה like a בעל אוב, so he fits the משנה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: חובר חבר covers gathering any creatures, big or small
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the איסור of חובר חבר applies to gathering large animals, small animals, and even snakes and scorpions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "חובר חבר" means gathering big creatures and gathering small creatures, and even snakes and scorpions.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 27 mentioned the חובר, so the גמרא now brings a ברייתא that defines how wide the איסור of חובר חבר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חבר means a gathering. The ברייתא teaches that the איסור does not depend on the size of the creatures being gathered. Big or small, and even dangerous creatures like snakes and scorpions, all count.

keyTerms.meaning: A charmer, someone who uses magic to gather creatures together

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "A charmer"
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק listing forbidden kinds of magic, דברים 18:11.

phrases.english: both a gathering of large creatures
and a gathering of small creatures,
and even snakes and scorpions.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״חֹבֵר חָבֶר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side discussion that defines the חובר category mentioned in steps 26 and 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The איסור of חובר חבר applies to gathering any creatures, whether large or small, even snakes and scorpions.

steps.title: אביי: gathering a hornet and scorpion is forbidden even for protection
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes from the ברייתא that magically gathering a hornet and a scorpion is אסור, even if the person only wants to stop them from causing harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Therefore, someone who magically gathers a hornet and a scorpion is doing something forbidden, even if he means only to keep them from doing harm.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the ברייתא and turns it into a practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that even snakes and scorpions count for חובר חבר. אביי learns from this that a good reason does not help. Even when the goal is protection, the act of gathering them through magic is still אסור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the איסור is about the act of magical gathering itself, not about whether the person wants to cause harm.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Therefore,
this one who gathers a hornet and a scorpion,
phrases.notes: He means gathering them by magic.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא מִיכַּוֵּין דְּלָא לַיזְּקוּ, אָסוּר.
phrases.english: even though he intends that they should not cause harm, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הִלְכָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical halacha from the ברייתא in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gathering a hornet and a scorpion through magic is אסור, even when the intention is only to prevent harm.

steps.title: Why is bowing an action but moving the lips is not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יוחנן and asks why, according to the רבנן, bending the body counts as an action but twisting the lips does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן, what is the difference? Why does bending one's body count as an action for the רבנן, but twisting one's lips does not count as an action?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier discussion of רבי יוחנן's approach and challenges the line he drew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יוחנן explained that according to the רבנן, someone who serves עבודה זרה by bowing is considered to have done an action. A מגדף, however, is not considered to have done one. The גמרא asks why this should be so: speaking also moves the lips, so it should count as an action just like bending the body does.

keyTerms.meaning: Bending one's body, as when bowing
Twisting or moving one's lips, as when speaking

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא is returning to רבי יוחנן's earlier explanation of the רבנן, after the side discussion about חובר חבר.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan, what is the difference
that bending one's height, according to the Rabbis, is an action,
phrases.notes: "Bending one's height" means bowing down to an idol.

phrases.english: but twisting his lips is not an action?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about חובר and returns to רבי יוחנן's earlier explanation of the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's distinction, according to the רבנן, between bowing (counts as an action) and blasphemy (does not)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both are small physical movements, so if bending the body counts as an action, moving the lips should count too.

steps.title: רבא: a מגדף is different because his sin is in the heart
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a מגדף is different, because his sin is also in the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A מגדף is different, since his sin is in the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from step 30 and explains why the מגדף is treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not say that moving the lips can never count as an action. He explains that the sin of a מגדף is mainly in the heart, in what he means, and not only in the lip movement. That is why the מגדף is an exception and does not bring a קרבן, while the one who bows does.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן's reading of the רבנן, bowing counts as an action. A מגדף is an exception, because his sin is rooted in the heart.

phrases.english: Rava said: A blasphemer is different,
since it is in the heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שָׁאנֵי מְגַדֵּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the מגדף is an exception because his sin depends on the heart
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since moving the lips is a physical movement just like bowing, it should count as an action.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blasphemy is different, because its sin is rooted in the heart, so it is not treated like an action for a קרבן.
